transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-12-16 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Carlos Ortega (MiramarTech CTO), Mei Lin (MiramarTech Security Engineer), Asha Patel (PM)

Summary:
Quick weekly check-in on POC security items: SSO/SAML integration, audit log export and retention, SOC2 scoping questions, KMS integration and encryption, and next steps for demo/benchmark. Some minor transcription errors present.

Topics:
- SSO / SAML metadata + SCIM
- Audit logs: fields, retention, exporter format
- Data retention policy and deletion controls
- SOC2 evidence timeline and scoping
- KMS/HSM integration for customer-managed keys
- Prod vs dedicated vs private VPC pilot options

Action items (captured above)

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: hey everyone, thanks for joining, I think we have about 45 minutes today, we'll run through the security checklist and any blockers for the pilot.
[00:12] Carlos Ortega: yeah thanks Jordan, quick FYI, CTO side I'll be on for the first half, then Mei will take over the sec details.
[00:20] Priya Nair: hi all, Priya from Redwood SE, I'll be running the audit-log tests this week.
[00:25] Mei Lin: hey, sounds good. we did try the initial SAML handshake yesterday, ran into a metadata attribute mismatch.
[00:33] Jordan Lee: okay can you say more about the mismatch? is it the email/uid mapping?
[00:38] Mei Lin: yeah the NameID format we send is urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:1.1:nameid-format:emailAddress and our IdP expects transient—so attributes like mail and uid weren't being passed.
[00:50] Carlos Ortega: we also need SCIM for group sync for RBAC, otherwise provisioning is a pain.
[00:56] Priya Nair: totally, we support SAML + SCIM—SCIM is in the pilot, we just need the attribute mapping and a SCIM token. I'll note that down.
[01:05] Asha Patel: and on retention, MiramarTech policy is 90 days by default for logs but certain PII must be purged after 30, so we need flexible retention windows.
[01:16] Jordan Lee: thanks Asha, Redwood can configure retention per-workspace and we have short/long windows; need to confirm the specific fields you consider PII.
[01:25] Mei Lin: fields are: user email, user id, raw prompt text in some cases, and customer metadata. We're trying to avoid long-term storage of prompt text.
[01:35] Priya Nair: note, our platform can redact prompts or not persist full prompt by default for customers that request that—there's also prefix caching (KV cache) but that's an implementation detail.
[01:45] Carlos Ortega: wait, when you say KV cache, is that K V cache? can that be disabled or kept in-memory only?
[01:51] Priya Nair: yes, sorry transcription-ish, KV cache: it's configurable, can be ephemeral in RAM and not persisted to disk; for private deployments we can also restrict disk writes.
[02:05] Jordan Lee: moving on to audit logs: Mei, can you confirm what fields you need in the audit log export?
[02:12] Mei Lin: at minimum: timestamp, request id, user id, route/model used, decision path (model variant), and a hash of the prompt if full prompt can't be retained. We'd like an integrity signature on exported logs.
[02:25] Priya Nair: we can include request_id, user_id, model, latency, token counts, and attach a SHA-256 hash of the prompt. Exports are JSONL and can be pushed to S3 or pulled via API.
[02:38] Carlos Ortega: S3 push is preferred; can we point to our S3 with a cross-account role?
[02:44] Priya Nair: yes, cross-account S3 push is supported; we also support syslog/ELK via our exporter. We'll run the exporter test and upload a sample.
[02:55] Asha Patel: great. about SOC2, what's Redwood's current status? we've seen some marketing claims but need timelines and scope.
[03:03] Jordan Lee: Redwood completed Type II SOC2 for core platform earlier this year, but we're in the process of expanding scope for private deployments. I'll share the scoping doc and a redacted report—note that the official Type II report is under NDA, we'll need an NDA to share that.
[03:18] Mei Lin: do you have pen-test results and third-party vuln scans?
[03:22] Jordan Lee: yes we have a pen-test summary, vuln remediation timeline; I'll include that in the pack.
[03:29] Carlos Ortega: KMS: we need customer-managed keys (CMK) for encryption at rest and separate key material. Is HSM supported?
[03:35] Priya Nair: we support KMS integrations with cloud KMS providers, and can do customer-managed keys; for private on-prem we can integrate with HSMs as well. We'll provide the KMS integration diagram.
[03:47] Mei Lin: ok show me where key rotation alerts surface and where audit logs for key usage are stored.
[03:53] Priya Nair: rotation events and key usage are logged to audit logs; we can push key usage logs to your S3 or to our SIEM integration.
[04:02] Jordan Lee: running through a few tradeoffs: hosted quickstart is fastest, but for stricter compliance you may prefer Redwood Private in a VPC or on-prem with customer KMS. That increases latency ops vs cost.
[04:15] Carlos Ortega: for the pilot we want to validate both SSO + audit logs on hosted with VPC peering; if that looks good we might move to dedicated or private for production.
[04:26] Priya Nair: that's a common path. For the benchmark we should run a short load test in your VPC to confirm latency targets and ensure batching doesn't leak PII across tenants.
[04:38] Asha Patel: about RBAC, can we map IdP groups to Redwood roles?
[04:43] Priya Nair: yes group-to-role mapping is supported via SCIM + a mapping table in the console; we'll share a sample mapping.
[04:51] Mei Lin: a couple of small asks: 1) sample audit logs with hashed prompt; 2) a template for the SAML attribute map; 3) examples of retention enforcement via API so we can run deletion tests.
[05:05] Jordan Lee: noted. We'll deliver 1-3 this week.
[05:09] Carlos Ortega: onboarding checklist—who is responsible for the SAML metadata exchange?
[05:13] Asha Patel: I'll coordinate and send the metadata to Jordan after we confirm the attribute map.
[05:18] Jordan Lee: perfect. Next, Mei mentioned wanting an integrity signature on exports—Priya can you outline how that is done?
[05:25] Priya Nair: we sign export files with a rotating signing key, and we can provide a public key to MiramarTech to verify signatures. The export includes a manifest with SHA256 hashes for each line.
[05:36] Mei Lin: that should work. Also we need to know retention enforcement timeline—if a user requests deletion, how quickly can data be purged?
[05:45] Priya Nair: deletion requests can be executed via API; for hosted setups we aim for sub-24-hour pipeline time to purge persisted prompt text if you opt-in. For private/dedicated it's under your control and typically immediate.
[05:58] Carlos Ortega: is there a documented SLA for deletion?
[06:02] Jordan Lee: we'll include deletion SLA language in the SOC2 scoping doc and the pilot agreement.
[06:09] Asha Patel: question on logs retention: can we do differential retention per field? e.g., keep metadata for 365 days but prompt text 30 days?
[06:18] Priya Nair: yes we support per-field retention policies via the retention matrix, and we can store hashed prompt references separately to maintain traceability.
[06:30] Mei Lin: good. on the topic of encryption in transit, do you support mutual TLS for internal service-to-service traffic?
[06:37] Priya Nair: yes mTLS is available for private deployments, for hosted we use TLS with strong cipher suites and we can arrange a dedicated peering with cert-based auth.
[06:48] Jordan Lee: ok shifting to timeline: Carlos, you said pilot success criteria include SSO + audit logs + retention enforcement—are there performance targets?
[06:58] Carlos Ortega: for the pilot we'd like p95 latency under 200ms for single-turn generation at 1 concurrent per user, and batch throughput test to hit our QPS.
[07:07] Priya Nair: we can run those in your VPC and we'll include a benchmark report. We'll also note the tradeoff if you enable aggressive persistence or longer sequences which may increase latency.
[07:19] Asha Patel: one more compliance ask—do you provide logs for admin actions (who created keys, who changed RBAC)?
[07:26] Priya Nair: yes admin activity is logged with user id, action, timestamp; these are part of the audit log stream.
[07:33] Jordan Lee: ok quick recap and next steps: Jordan to share SOC2 scoping doc + redacted report request instructions; Priya to run audit-log exporter test and upload sample; Priya/Jordan to send SAML attribute mapping template; Carlos/Asha to send SAML metadata and confirm retention matrix; schedule VPC benchmark.
[07:50] Carlos Ortega: sounds good. we'll aim to get the metadata and retention matrix this week.
[07:55] Mei Lin: thanks all, will review the sample logs once uploaded.
[08:00] Jordan Lee: thanks everyone, I'll send notes and the deck link now.
